subject: Auto Mechanics
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice questions in 1 hour for 40 marks. Paper 2: five essay questions, answer any four, in 1 1/2 hours for 60 marks. Paper 3: two practical tests, both carried out, in 2 hours for 100 marks; schools supply the materials locally.

topics.name: Workshop Regulations and Safety
objectives: Apply basic safety rules relating to personnel, tools, equipment and environment
Identify the types of fire extinguishers: foam, dry powder, sand, water and wet-blanket types
topics.content: Practical: identification and use of safety devices (aprons, goggles, shield, etc.); demonstration and use of fire extinguishers.

topics.name: Basic Tools, Instruments and Equipment
objectives: Use basic tools, e.g. hand tools and power tools
Use measuring instruments
Use basic equipment, e.g. jacks, hoist, air-compressors
topics.content: Practical: identification and use of basic tools, measuring instruments and basic equipment.

topics.name: Layout of a Motor Vehicle
objectives: Describe the layout of a conventional motor vehicle
State the functions of the main components
Describe drive arrangements: front engine rear wheel drive, rear engine rear wheel drive, front engine front wheel drive, four-wheel drive
topics.content: Practical: inspection of the layout and drive arrangements of a motor vehicle; identification of the main components.

topics.name: Engine
objectives: Classify engines (petrol and diesel) and name their main parts

State the arrangement and functions of the main components: cylinder head and cover, cylinder block, crankshaft, flywheel, connecting rod, piston and rings, spark plug (petrol), fuel injection pump and injector (diesel), valve, valve springs, oil seal, camshaft, push rod, rocker shaft/arms
Describe two stroke and four stroke cycle petrol and diesel engines
State the advantages and disadvantages of petrol and diesel engines
Distinguish single and multi-cylinder engines
Describe crank arrangement and firing orders: 2, 4 and 6 cylinder in-line engines, V-4, V-6 and 4-cylinder horizontally-opposed engines
Describe the functions and operation of valve operating mechanisms, drives layout and main components of a 4-cylinder 12- and 16-valve engine
Explain valve timing, including calculation of valve opening and closing periods
topics.content: Practical: identification of main components; decarbonization of cylinder head; identification of two and four stroke engines; classification of engines by cylinders; compression test; measurement of bore and crank-journals for wear; determination of firing order through valve opening; valve adjustments; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Fuel Supply Systems
objectives: Explain fuels and combustion: elements of combustion, air-fuel ratios, types and properties of petrol and diesel

Describe the layout and operation of the petrol supply system: gravity and force-feed systems, simple carburetor, multi-jet carburetor, air filters/cleaners, mechanical and electrical fuel pumps and their advantages and disadvantages
Describe the petrol-injection system, its merits and demerits, and electronic fuel injection (EFI)
Describe the layout of a diesel supply system, with elementary treatment of injection pumps and injectors
Describe cold starting devices
topics.content: Practical: checking fuel system troubles; inspection of exhaust gases for normal air-fuel ratios and excessively worn engine; dismantling, examination and reassembling of a mechanical fuel pump and carburetors; fault diagnosis; identification of main components; inspection of injection pumps, servicing of injectors and bleeding.

topics.name: Exhaust System
objectives: State the purpose and layout of the exhaust system
Identify the types of silencers and manifolds
topics.content: Practical: inspection of the exhaust system; identification of exhaust and inlet manifolds; checking the system for leakage.

topics.name: Lubrication
objectives: State the reasons for lubrication and the types: boundary layer and film lubrication
Identify lubricated parts and components
Describe the types of feed: splash, forced and petroil (wet and dry)
Explain the principle of operation of gear and rotor oil pumps and oil filters
Describe lubricants and their applications in engines, transmission, steering, suspension system and doors
Explain viscosity rating and SAE numbers
topics.content: Practical: identification of main components; changing oil and oil filters; servicing and testing of pumps; fault diagnosis; identification of different types of lubricants; comparing fresh and used oil; use of grease gun and oil can.

topics.name: Cooling System
objectives: Explain the process of heat transfer
Describe the water cooling system: purpose, layout, functions of main components, thermo-syphon and pump assisted systems, elementary treatment of pressurized cooling system
State the purpose and types of thermostats (bellows and wax pellet)
Describe the air cooling system: layout, functions and main components
Compare the air and water cooled systems
topics.content: Practical: identification of main components; inspection of radiator and its construction; replacement of fan belt and hoses; flushing; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Transmission System
objectives: State the function and layout of the transmission system and its types, manual and automatic (excluding twin axles and double reduction axles), with merits and demerits
Explain the functions of a clutch, the types and operating principles of single plate and multiplate clutches, and the methods of actuation (hydraulic and mechanical), with simple calculations
Describe automatic transmission (introduction) and the functions of the torque converter and fluid flywheel
Describe the types, layout and operating principles of sliding-mesh, constant mesh and synchromesh gearboxes, their main components, the gear selector mechanism and simple calculations of gear ratios
State the functions and types of the propeller shaft, universal joint and sliding joint
State the purpose of the rear axle and the arrangement and functions of its main components: final drive, differential unit, half-shaft, oil seal and hub bearings
Describe methods of supporting axle shafts and their advantages and disadvantages
topics.content: Practical: identification of layouts; dismantling, identifying parts and re-assembling a single plate clutch; adjusting clutch pedal clearance and bleeding; identification of gearbox components and inspection of gear teeth for wear; examination of propeller shaft and universal joint bearings for bow and wear; identification of rear axle components; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Wheels and Tyres
objectives: Describe the types of wheel rims: pressed steel, disc and wire spoke wheels
Describe hub attachments
Distinguish tubed and tubeless tyres and state their advantages and disadvantages
Explain wheel balancing, tyre sizes and markings
topics.content: Practical: checking and adjustment of wheel bearing clearance; removal and changing of road wheels; tyre fitting and checking tyre pressure; tube and tyre patching; wheel balancing.

topics.name: Braking System
objectives: Describe the layout, functions and operation of the braking system: drum and disc, mechanical and hydraulic
Describe brake lining materials and methods of attachment
State the importance of servo-assisted brakes
State the advantages and disadvantages of disc and drum brakes
Diagnose brake faults
topics.content: Practical: inspection of different types of brakes; replacement of pads and shoes, bleeding and adjustment; spot-testing of brakes; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Steering System
objectives: Describe the general layout and functions of the front axle and steering systems
Explain steering geometry: Ackerman linkage, castor, camber, king pin inclination, toe-in and toe-out
Describe the types of steering gearbox: rack and pinion and recirculating ball only
Diagnose steering faults
topics.content: Practical: identification of main components of different layouts; front wheel alignment; inspection of tyre wear patterns; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Suspension System
objectives: State the purpose, layout and types of suspension: rigid beam and independent
Describe suspension springs (semi-elliptic and coil springs), their advantages and disadvantages, and dampers (shock absorbers)
topics.content: Practical: identification of differences between rigid beam and independent suspension; fault diagnosis.

topics.name: Electrical Systems
topics.content: Practical items include setting up simple electrical circuits and using simple measuring instruments; simple soldering and joining of cables; examination and testing of a lead-acid battery and preparing electrolyte; ignition timing and setting contact breaker points and spark plug gaps; inspection and replacement of bulbs and fuses; head lamp focusing; electrical fault diagnosis.

subtopics.name: Fundamentals of electrical systems
objectives: Explain basic electrical terms and symbols, a.c. and d.c. sources, simple circuits
Apply Ohm's law in calculations involving series and parallel circuits
State the functions of basic components: relays, resistors, lamps, fuses and switches

subtopics.name: Auto wiring system
objectives: State the reasons for wire gauges and colour coding
Describe the wiring system: earth and insulated returns
Describe ways of joining cables: jointing, terminals, connectors and soldering

subtopics.name: Battery (motor vehicle)
objectives: Explain the purpose, construction and testing of the lead-acid battery
State the electrolyte composition
Describe battery care and maintenance

subtopics.name: Ignition system (coil)
objectives: Describe the layout of the coil ignition system and the function and operation of its main components
Describe computerized ignition systems (introduction)

subtopics.name: Starting system (motor vehicle)
objectives: Describe the layout and functions of the main components
Identify the types of starter motor

subtopics.name: Charging system (motor vehicle)
objectives: State the purpose and layout of the charging system (dynamo and alternator)
Describe the main components and their operation
Compare d.c. and a.c. generators

subtopics.name: Lighting system (motor vehicle)
objectives: Describe the layout of the system, main components and their functions
Identify the types and ratings of fuses and bulbs

subtopics.name: Auxiliary unit
objectives: Describe the layout and operation of the auxiliary units: instrument panel, horn, windscreen wiper
Identify electrical faults

topics.name: Electronics
topics.content: Practical: identification of components; identification of components in single-point and multi-point injection systems.

subtopics.name: Fundamentals of electronics
objectives: Explain the term auto electronics
Identify electronic components: diodes, transistors, resistors, capacitors, LED, transducers, coil and motors
State the functions of components and their symbols in a circuit

subtopics.name: Electronic ignition
objectives: Describe the operation of the transistorized ignition system
Distinguish the types of transistorized and electronic ignition system: inductive and hall effect, with merits and demerits

subtopics.name: Electronic fuel injection
objectives: State the purpose and types of systems: single-point and multi-point injections

topics.name: Auto Air-Conditioning
objectives: State the purpose, layout and identification of major components (compressor, condenser, evaporator and dryer)
Explain the principles of operation
topics.content: Practical: inspection and identification of the air-conditioning system and its components.

topics.name: Safe Motoring
objectives: State the main causes of accident, the essentials of safe driving, and the application of the highway code and safety devices
topics.content: Practical: identification of faults and defective components that could cause accidents; identification and interpretation of road signs.
